newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Pertamina, Japan firms to finalise Natuna stake.
newsitem.headline: Pertamina, Japan firms to finalise Natuna stake.

text.p: Indonesian state oil company Pertamina said on Tuesday negotiations with several Japanese firms over a stake in the country's giant Natuna natural gas project were expected to conclude with an agreement early next year.
"We are still discussing the Natuna stake with several Japanese firms. But the negotiations are almost finalised," Pertamina's general affairs director Baharuddin told reporters.
"I expect the talks will be concluded next January and then we will sign the deal as soon as possible," he said.
"The possibility is that Japanese firms will take a stake of between 11 percent to 13 percent in Natuna."
Baharuddin said Pertamina wanted to reduce its current 24 percent stake in the project to 11 percent.
He said the Japanese firms involved in the talks included Nissho Iwai Corp, Mitsubishi Corp and Mitsui and Co Ltd.

In July, Pertamina granted Mobil Corp a 26 percent stake in the Natuna field, which is estimated to hold 210 trillion cubic feet (tcf) of gas, of which 45 tcf are thought to be commercially recoverable.
Exxon Corp holds the remaining 50 percent share of the project.
